lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in last 24 months is the 1858 A Kuenker hammer EUR 360 = AUD 584 (the 1859 sales are a different date at an older gold price, so not used). 584 / 1.198 = 487, rounded down to 485. All-in at 485 is AUD 581, about coin melt (AUD 557) plus a little for the pin. Because lot 152 is mounted, worn and has a solder spot, 485 is a ceiling, not a target. Flip: likely resale about AUD 580 (Kuenker sale; mounted coins rarely beat that), less 13% selling fees (eBay or online auction) and AUD 15 registered post: 580 x 0.87 - 15 = 489.6; / 2.396 = 204, rounded down to 200. Current bid is already $460, so a flip is not viable. Pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.

lots.key_photo_findings: Obverse reads NAPOLEON III EMPEREUR, bare head, BARRE signature; reverse EMPIRE FRANCAIS, 10 FRANCS 1858, A mint mark, laurel wreath. Pin is a simple wire bar passing across the reverse (a wire C-clasp and pointed pin), not a bezel. Enlarged crop shows a greyish rough spot right of the 10 on the reverse, near FRANCS, consistent with solder or a residue where the pin was attached. Rims show light knocks; wire slightly bent.
lots.condition: Coin worn (about VF), clear legends, solder or blemish spot on reverse, mounted; pin slightly bent. Carat of the pin not visible in photos.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is the pin stamped 18ct, and what does the coin weigh on its own (or how is it attached: soldered or clipped)? Can the pin be removed without damaging the coin?

lots.what_it_is: Unmarked yellow gold necklace in the Georgian or Etruscan revival style: eleven graduated oval cabochon garnet-type stones in rope-twist wire collets, each with a gold rosette set with a seed pearl, a drop pendant with a larger cabochon in a border of small pearls or white stones, triple fine trace chains and a small cabochon clasp. Gowans: unmarked 9ct, 15ct and 18ct gold, some stones cracked, dented back, 62.9 g total, 50 cm. Presented in a modern 'for the Love of Gold' retail box. Age not established; could be antique or a later revival or reproduction. Current bid $1,000 (1 bid) when fetched 30 Sep 2026.
